summary: Every paper against you: Every outlet in {the place} has endorsed {rival}, and {staffer} says the campaign needs its own way to reach people.
realLife: One life: In the 1928 Louisiana governor's race he used sound trucks and radio ads; running for the Senate in 1930 with all of the state's daily papers backing his opponent, he started his own paper. Another: In the 1934 California governor's race the big Hearst and Chandler papers attacked him throughout.
gates: The outlets on record have endorsed {rival}.
weights: How spread out the place is.
choices: start your own paper or sheet
buy radio time or sound trucks
go town to town in person

branches.then: It becomes a record of what you said that reporters can quote back.

branches.when: the papers run your old words
branches.then: The attacks become a daily box of your own lines.
